messages.author: 2c38ab32c3b498d5
messages.subject: "Lite" version of mirt package
parts:
Hi Phill,

I am using the mirt package within an RScript on my application that is called through command line as part of the workflow. However, when the overall execution time of the RScript takes ~4s, 2 of them are only loading up the lattice package, which as I understand serves only for visualization purposes. Since this step is run many times during the workflow (and the RScript has to load the packages everytime) this causes too much overhead.

 I wonder if you could point me what is absolutely required to run the following commands:

mirt(data, 1, itemtype="3PL", TOL=1e-5, pars="values")
mirt(data, 1, itemtype="3PL", TOL=1e-5, pars=pars)
fscores(irtmodel, method="EAP", full.scores=T)
fscores(irtmodel, response.patterns=patterns, method="EAP", full.scores=F)

This way I could save a lot of processing on the backend.

Thanks!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: "Lite" version of mirt package
parts:
Seems like a dangerous thing to do, but I suppose you could play around with the source code imports until it works. Download a version of the package source code (from CRAN or Github) and edit the files DESCRIPTION and NAMESPACE. 

In DESCRIPTION, delete the depends: and imports: elements (probably all of them), and in NAMESPACE remove all the import() elements except for those relating to the S4 and Rcpp. Then, install this package on your R system with 'R CMD INSTALL mirt' to replace your current working version. 

That should work, though it's definitely not kosher. Cheers.

Phil
